title: Powers of the Central Government — Section 3 EPA

content.overview: Section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 empowers the Central Government to take all such measures as it deems necessary or expedient for the purpose of protecting and improving the quality of the environment and preventing, controlling and abating environmental pollution. The section lists illustrative measures, including coordination, planning, standards, restriction of areas, procedures and safeguards, and examination of manufacturing processes.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Central Government measure under s. 3? (2) Purpose — protect/improve environment or prevent/control/abate pollution? (3) Connected ss. 7–8, 15, 19? (4) Forum for challenge?
content.study:
s. 3 is the principal enabling provision for Central action under the EPA. It supports rules, notifications, standards and directions. Penalties and process offences are separate (e.g. s. 15). Consent and sector statutes (Water Act, Air Act) may still apply on the facts.

No new case invented. Cases present in related environment files (Vellore, M.C. Mehta) remain for doctrinal context only when the issue matches.

sections.heading: Enabling power
sections.body: Central Government may take all measures necessary or expedient to protect and improve environmental quality and to prevent, control and abate pollution.

sections.heading: Illustrative measures
sections.body: Coordination between authorities; planning and execution of nationwide programmes; laying down standards; restriction of areas; procedures and safeguards; examination of processes and materials — as enacted in s. 3(2).

sections.heading: Connected provisions
sections.body: ss. 7–8 (persons carrying on industry not to allow emission/discharge beyond standards; handling of hazardous substances); s. 15 (penalty); s. 19 (cognizance).

sections.heading: Subordinate legislation
sections.body: Rules and notifications under the EPA flow from this enabling frame; always match the specific instrument to the power claimed.

sections.heading: Forum
sections.body: NGT for specified environmental disputes; High Court under Art. 226; Supreme Court under Arts. 32/136 as maintainable.

provisions.title: Power of Central Government to take measures to protect and improve environment

examples.title: Standards notification
examples.body: Central Government lays down emission standards for an industry class under s. 3 powers — operators must comply; breach may attract penalty and directions under connected provisions.

hypotheticals.question: Is every environmental direction automatically valid under s. 3?
hypotheticals.analysis: The measure must fall within the purpose of protecting/improving the environment or preventing/controlling/abating pollution and within the statutory scheme; ultra vires and procedural challenges remain available.

distinctions.title: s. 3 powers vs s. 15 penalty
distinctions.left: Enabling measures by the Central Government.
distinctions.right: Penal consequence for contravention of the Act, rules, orders or directions.

misconceptions.trap: s. 3 replaces the Water Act and Air Act entirely.
misconceptions.correction: s. 3 is an EPA enabling power; Water and Air Acts remain sector statutes and may apply concurrently on the facts.
